FreightWaves announced the winners of its Shipper of Choice awards on Monday, Oct. 26, at the F3: Future of Freight Festival, recognizing companies that stand out for their relationships with freight carriers and their approach to shipping operations.
Craig Fuller, founder and CEO of FreightWaves and SONAR, presented the awards during the F3 Awards Dinner at The Signal in Chattanooga.
The award evaluates shippers across several areas, including data connectivity, ease of doing business, carrier relationships and facility operations. Industry voting determines the winners, with an emphasis on the practices that make companies preferred partners for trucking carriers.
These factors can affect how efficiently carriers move freight. Long waits at shipping and receiving facilities, unreliable scheduling and complicated administrative processes can cut into drivers’ productive hours and limit the number of loads they can complete.
The winning shippers were recognized for taking steps to address those challenges and improve conditions for the carriers moving their freight.
“All of them have made investments to improve the lives of our drivers,” Fuller said. “(They’ve) gone out of their way to improve the lives of the carriers and their operators.”
Here’s a glimpse into the honorees:
Schreiber Foods
Schreiber Foods, a dairy and food manufacturer, emphasizes long-term carrier relationships and predictable freight procurement. The company holds its annual freight bid at the same time each year, regardless of market conditions, and prioritizes the carriers already moving its freight.
Schreiber also trains plant employees on drivers’ hours-of-service rules, uses drop trailers to reduce detention and pays most carriers on net-35-to-45-day terms.
Kraft Heinz
Kraft Heinz focuses on regular communication and transparency with its carrier partners. The food and beverage company holds weekly scorecard calls, conducts in-person business reviews and collects anonymous carrier feedback more frequently than quarterly.
The company also works to handle detention and layovers fairly. It has brought carriers into the development process for a new claims intake portal, giving transportation partners an opportunity to test the system.
Aldi USA
Aldi USA earned recognition for predictable facility operations and reliable appointment scheduling. One carrier moves about 150 loads a week into the grocery retailer and reports detention on only a handful of shipments.
The company also provides clear feedback on freight bids, helping carriers understand where they stand when competing for business.
Whole Foods Market
Whole Foods Market stands out for facility efficiency and its approach to food safety. Carriers report that unloading typically takes less than two hours, while the retailer shares research-backed practices designed to protect product quality.
One example involves data-backed transit temperature guidance for cherries intended to extend shelf life. Whole Foods also rewards consistent service with long-term business relationships, including one carrier partner that has hauled a key portion of its turkey program for three consecutive years.
Sealed Air
Packaging company Sealed Air has invested in drop-trailer pools, cross-border transportation and API connections for tracking and billing.
Its approach to carrier relationships also includes flexibility when operational problems arise. In one instance, a plant changed its operating hours so a driver who had traveled 400 miles with the wrong freight could return and correct the mistake.
Agri-Mark/Cabot Creamery
Agri-Mark, the farmer-owned cooperative behind Cabot Creamery, emphasizes appointment flexibility and responsiveness. Drivers typically spend about 45 minutes at its facilities, and carriers can book or change appointments through an online portal.
The company also responds to carriers on weekends and operates a quoting tool that shows how their rates compare with market prices.
North American Stainless
North American Stainless honors contracted rates and volumes even when spot-market prices are lower. The steel producer also offers drop-and-hook operations and preloaded trailers at no cost to carriers, an uncommon arrangement for flatbed freight.
The company pays carriers on net-30 terms and assigns each carrier a dedicated logistics coordinator.
Henkel
Henkel, a global manufacturer of adhesives, sealants and consumer products including Loctite and Persil, was recognized for its data connectivity and relationships with transportation partners. Its North American operations span industrial and consumer markets, requiring coordination across a diverse supply chain.
Nestlé USA
Nestlé USA was recognized for its distribution network and supply chain relationships, which help the company coordinate deliveries and support retail partners. The company often takes on some of retailers’ distribution and logistics responsibilities, helping maintain a reliable flow of products.
Univar Solutions
Univar Solutions distributes chemicals and ingredients, including solvents, resins and surfactants, to industries ranging from agriculture to pharmaceuticals. Its operations combine a broad distribution network with logistics and formulation services.
The company emphasizes data-connected supply chains and collaboration with transportation partners to coordinate freight movement across its network.
Why this matters
Shipper practices can directly affect trucking efficiency, from the time drivers spend waiting at facilities to how easily carriers manage appointments, payments and freight scheduling. Companies that prioritize predictable operations and strong carrier relationships can help reduce delays, protect drivers’ productive hours and build more reliable transportation networks. The Shipper of Choice awards recognize businesses making those practices a priority.

Astellas Pharma could secure the exclusive global rights to Audax Biosciences’ DAX-044, an antibody-cytokine fusion therapy that activates the immune system in the vicinity of the tumor.
Astellas Pharma is inking a deal worth up to $1.34 billion biobucks for the exclusive option to license an investigational immuno-oncology candidate from Audax Biosciences, which the Japanese drugmaker hopes to advance for solid tumors.
Astellas could pay Audax an undisclosed upfront payment plus potential option exercise fee totaling $285 million if the drugmaker chooses to develop the antibody-cytokine fusion DAX-044. Audax’s asset is designed to work by concentrating the immune-activating action of the IL-12 cytokine in the vicinity of the tumor, limiting systemic toxicities associated with IL-12 therapies, according to a Tuesday news release .
Under the terms of the deal, Melbourne-based Audax could additionally stand to receive up to $1.05 billion in development and commercial milestones, and is eligible for tiered double-digit royalties on worldwide net sales of DAX-044. All told, the deal could reach $1.34 billion in value.
Audax last year started research that could enable a regulatory filing seeking permission to push DAX-044 into clinical development. The biotech will be responsible for funding the asset into Phase 1 development, which is expected to start in 2027. Astellas could then assume global development, manufacturing and commercialization of DAX-044, though Audax will have the option to co-fund and co-promote the asset in Australia and New Zealand.
“DAX-044 is a promising investigational immuno-oncology program with a differentiated mechanism designed to selectively activate anti-tumor immune responses,” Takahiko Iwaya, chief strategy officer at Astellas, said in a prepared statement. “[W]e hope to advance a potential new treatment option for patients with solid tumors, including cancers where effective immune stimulation remains an important therapeutic challenge.”

CATL hit another milestone in its solid-state battery development, advancing to 20 Ah cells. The world’s leading battery maker aims to begin small-scale production in 2027.
CATL continues advancing solid-state EV batteries
CATL remains the leading global EV battery manufacturer by a wide margin. According to SNE Research , CATL held a commanding 39.9% share of the global EV battery market through the first half of 2026.
To stay ahead, the company is advancing several new battery chemistries, including solid-state and sodium-ion, promising to be safer, more efficient, and lower cost than traditional lithium-ion batteries.
When investors asked about the progress of its solid-state battery program on Tuesday, CATL said it continues to invest heavily in all-solid-state batteries and expects to begin small-scale production in 2027.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
As it has stated before, output is expected to be limited at first as it scales up to mass production around 2030.
Speaking at the Summer Davos Forum in June, CATL chairman and CEO Robin Zeng said that, on a scale of one to nine, all-solid-state batteries have only reached level four.
All-solid-state batteries differ from semi-solid-state batteries in that they require a solid electrolyte to conduct lithium ions, rather than a liquid.
Dr Wu Kai, CATL’s chief scientist (Source: CATL)
The company uses a sulfide-based solid electrolyte system, which offers high ionic conductivity and deformability, but maintaining stable contact between solid components remains a hurdle.
CATL said its sulfide-based batteries have now entered 20 Ah trial production as it aims to achieve an energy density of 500 Wh/kg.
Trial production in 2027, reaching mass market in 2030
CATL’s 2027 timeline to begin small-scale production aligns with other automakers and battery manufacturers racing to introduce all-solid-state EV batteries.
Toyota, which has been promising solid-state batteries for nearly a decade now, aims to launch the first all-solid-state battery-powered EV in 2027 or 2028.
Toyota EV battery roadmap (Source: Toyota)
Using Sumitomo Metal Mining’s proprietary powder synthesis technology, Toyota claimed to have developed a “highly durable cathode material” for all-solid-state batteries last October. Toyota revealed a prototype last year, claiming it can deliver 745 miles (1,200 km) of range and charge in under 10 minutes.
However, like CATL, Toyota expects production to be limited and will not reach the mass market until closer to the end of the decade.
(Source: Toyota)
Samsung SDI, on the other hand, aims to begin mass production of its SolidStack all-solid-state batteries in the second half of 2027.
BYD, which ranks second in global EV battery sales behind CATL, also plans to launch its first solid-state battery-powered vehicle in 2027.
In an exclusive interview with Carwow.es last month, executive vice president Stella Li said BYD is in “the leading position” on solid-state batteries and will “prove that” next year.
BYD’s battery division, FinDreams, aims to begin producing sulfide-based all-solid-state batteries in limited batches in 2027, ramping up to mass production by 2030.
Electrek’s Take
While solid-state batteries are often hailed the “holy grail” of battery tech, they are only one part of the equation.
CATL, BYD, and others continue advancing lithium iron phosphate (LFP) and sodium-ion batteries, which will ultimately create more efficient, lower-cost options that offer various performance needs.
BYD’s second-generation Blade LFP batteries already deliver over 1,000 km (621 miles) of CLTC range. What’s next?
One thing is certain: New battery chemistries and evolving tech will only continue making EVs more efficient, unlocking longer driving ranges, faster charging speeds, and better performance.

Bracco plans to invest $230 million in its first U.S. manufacturing facility for injectable contrast media, selecting Sanford, North Carolina, for a project expected to create 200 jobs .
What’s Related
The sterile manufacturing plant will add production in the United States, Bracco’s largest market, to a network that already includes facilities in Europe, Asia, and Canada . Contrast media are used in diagnostic imaging to help doctors see inside the body.
Bracco said the additional space will help meet growing demand and make supplies more reliable for U.S. customers. North Carolina officials said the plant is expected to shorten delivery times and reduce transportation costs.
The planned jobs span manufacturing, engineering, technical operations, quality, warehousing and administration.

From Milan to North Carolina
“Producing injectable contrast media here in Sanford brings our supply closer to American hospitals and patients and makes it even more resilient ,” said Fulvio Renoldi Bracco, vice chairman and CEO of Bracco Imaging.
The Milan-based company cited North Carolina’s workforce and established life sciences industry as reasons for choosing Sanford. The Sanford Area Growth Alliance said the community competed with other domestic and international locations for the investment.
According to the alliance, the facility is expected to be fully staffed by 2031. State officials said the new positions could generate more than $20.6 million in annual payroll for the region.
State grant depends on hiring
North Carolina approved a Job Development Investment Grant for Bracco Imaging Operations USA LLC that could reimburse the company up to $2,859,300 over 12 years. Payments depend on annual verification that Bracco has met its job creation and investment targets.
The state estimates the project could add $1.78 billion to North Carolina’s economy over the grant’s term. The agreement also calls for directing up to $317,700 to a state fund that helps rural communities pay for infrastructure improvements.
Project partners include Central Carolina Community College, the North Carolina Community College System, state workforce officials, Lee County, the city of Sanford, and Duke Energy.

28 October 2026
The global express and parcels market grew 5.8% in 2025, to €577.3bn ($642.6bn), but mounting pricing pressure, shifting trade flows and intensifying competition are creating a growing challenge for carriers seeking to turn higher volumes into profits.
The recent Global Express & Parcels 2026 report by Transport Intelligence predicted that the market would reach €609.1bn this year and €760.1bn by 2030, representing compound annual growth of around 5.7%.
But the headline growth masks stark regional differences.
Asia Pacific, which in 2024 overtook North America as the largest regional market, is forecast to expand at an annual rate of 8% between 2026 and 2030, while North America is expected to grow 4.1%, and Europe by 3.6%, with several major carriers in mature markets experiencing revenue declines.
DHL Express told The Loadstar international cross-border express, particularly time-definite services, remained a growth engine for the group, although its premium proposition was not suited to every B2C shipment.
The company reported continued strong volumes into Europe and an uplift in shipments to Latin America, as retailers adjusted their strategies following the removal of the US de minimis exemption for low-value packages. Asia-US B2C volumes, which initially declined after the change, subsequently partially recovered.
under its Strategy 2030, DHL Express identified 22 markets with above-average growth potential, including Vietnam, Thailand, Poland, Mexico, Turkey, Brazil, and India, citing opportunities linked to near-shoring, supply chain diversification, and investment.
Ti report author Paul Chapman said: “The global parcels market continues to grow, but this masks increasingly divergent performance among operators, particularly in mature markets where pricing pressure, subdued B2B demand, and the shift towards lower-cost services are weighing on revenues.”
He added that established carriers faced the challenge of converting rising parcel volumes into profitable growth amid intensifying competition and the expansion of in-house delivery networks.
This has meant consolidation gathering pace. Ti tracked 136 mergers, acquisitions and investment transactions between May 2023 and August 2026, including the FedEx-Advent consortium’s €7.8bn agreement to take InPost private. Meanwhile, 24 of 34 identified artificial intelligence use cases in express and parcels are already operational.
On margins, DHL Express told The Loadstar it maintained a strong focus on yield and cost management, arguing that customers continued to pay for speed, reliability, security, and customs expertise.
A spokesperson said: “One area where we have seen a significant increase is in heavier-weight goods, with customers that previously might have favoured a forwarding-air cargo solution choosing DHL Express, based on factors such as the guaranteed uplift and capacity, reduced time for inventory in transit, reliable end-to-end delivery and visibility, and transparent, predictable pricing.”

Tesla’s new rocket-shaped Robotaxi service area in Houston includes parts of downtown where the service won’t actually pick you up, according to Ethan McKanna, the creator of Robotaxi Tracker and former Tesla employee.
McKanna rode the service after Monday’s expansion and called Houston “by far the most egregious ‘fake’ AV service area” he has seen. One trip quote had him spending about 40 minutes in a Robotaxi to go two blocks.
On Monday, Tesla expanded its Houston Robotaxi geofence into the shape of a rocket . It took the small launch zone in northwest Harris County and stretched it into a long corridor down to downtown and Bellaire, announced with “Houston, we have liftoff.”
McKanna runs Robotaxi Tracker, the crowdsourced site that tracks Tesla’s Robotaxi fleet and service areas, and he worked at Tesla this summer, so he knows the program better than most. He went to Houston to try it out. Here’s what he posted last night:
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Another thing. Often AV service area maps advertised are kind of fake- they don’t actually go to everywhere in the polygon the provider publishes. Robotaxi Houston is probably by far the most egregious ‘fake’ AV service area I’ve seen I get they were doing it so they could get… https://t.co/ILXIkmwGVp pic.twitter.com/yUfswZhQKF — Ethan McKanna (@ethanmckanna) October 28, 2026
The video shows the Robotaxi app with a pickup pin dropped in downtown Houston, well inside the polygon Tesla published. The app refuses it: “Location not available. Move the map to select a different location.”
McKanna acknowledged that AV service area maps are often “kind of fake,” since operators don’t serve every street inside the polygon they advertise. But he singled out Houston as the worst case he’s seen and said he understands Tesla did it “so they could get the starship shape,” which doesn’t seem like a good reason to fake availability.
About 40 minutes to go two blocks
The day before, he posted a trip quote that shows what this looks like for a rider:
40 min ride to cross 2 blocks downtown. this is pretty rough pic.twitter.com/n8kP4s9evT — Ethan McKanna (@ethanmckanna) October 26, 2026
The app quoted a 2:05 pm pickup on the east side of downtown and a 2:48 pm drop-off at Houston Police Department headquarters on Travis Street, a couple of blocks away. Instead of cutting across downtown, the planned route runs south through Midtown and the Museum District to the Texas Medical Center area, then loops back north.
McKanna’s read is that the Robotaxi appears to be avoiding railroad crossings downtown, and he said it fits with “other strange routing in Houston.” He expects Tesla to fix it.
To be fair, he wasn’t down on the service overall. He wrote that, apart from that issue, it “feels really good in Houston,” with reasonable wait times and “significantly better driving than my recent Waymo rides.”
Waymo’s map isn’t perfect either
Tesla isn’t the only one. On Tuesday, Robotaxi Tracker reported that Waymo’s Orlando service area had shrunk by 10 square miles, down 8.4% to 109 square miles. McKanna explained what happened:
Someone accidentally added the airport 😭 — Ethan McKanna (@ethanmckanna) October 27, 2026
Orlando’s airport was inside the map Waymo published, but McKanna checked the app and it won’t let riders set the airport as a drop-off yet. So the tracker took it out. Waymo’s airport service might be rolling out soon, and someone got ahead of the announcement.
That’s an airport on the edge of the map. In Houston, the dead zone is in the middle of downtown.
Electrek’s Take
First, a big thanks to Ethan. Tesla shares very little data about its Robotaxi program, and Robotaxi Tracker has become the best independent source on where Tesla’s fleet actually operates and how big it is. And as Orlando shows, he holds Waymo to the same standard.
Every AV operator has gaps in its map, Waymo included. But Waymo’s Orlando gap is an airport on the edge of the map that it’s likely about to add. Tesla’s Houston gap is downtown, and it drew a rocket first and figured out where the cars could actually go second.
Service and product should always outrank marketing, and that’s clearly not the case with Tesla’s Robotaxi. People rely on those maps to know if Tesla offers the service where they are. Faking the map just to make a rocket shape is completely stupid. Do better.

General Motors will prepare its Lansing Delta Township Assembly plant in Michigan to build hybrid vehicles, the company announced. The plant currently builds three gas-powered, three-row SUVs: the Buick Enclave, Chevrolet Traverse and GMC Acadia.
What’s Related
The hybrid plan is part of a bigger commitment to the area. GM said its investments in the Lansing region will top $2 billion over the next several years. That total includes $1.25 billion GM announced earlier for its Lansing Grand River Assembly plant.
GM hasn’t said which hybrids the plant will build or when production will start. It said model names and timing will come closer to launch. Reuters, citing unnamed sources, reported that the factory will produce hybrid versions of the Traverse, Enclave and Acadia. GM hasn’t confirmed that.
Federal money moves to hybrids
To help pay for the work, GM and the U.S. Department of Energy are restructuring a federal grant previously awarded to GM. The money, from DOE’s Domestic Manufacturing Conversion Grant program, will now go toward hybrid production at Lansing Delta Township.
TechCrunch reported that the grant was originally $500 million. The Biden administration awarded it to convert a different Lansing factory to build electric vehicles . GM told the outlet the money was never paid out.

A record year in Lansing
The plant turns 20 this year. It built more than 291,000 vehicles in 2025, its highest yearly total. GM didn’t say whether the hybrid work will add jobs .
“Lansing’s strength starts with its people. Their skill and experience are why we continue to invest here,” said Mike Trevorrow, GM’s senior vice president of Global Manufacturing. “We’re building on what this team does well today while preparing for what customers will need in the years ahead.”
He added, “That means investing in our people, our facilities, and the ability to build a broad range of vehicles.”
GM to spend more on U.S. manufacturing
GM expects to spend about $9 billion on U.S. manufacturing and more than $7 billion on U.S. research and development this year. It has also confirmed investments at Orion Assembly in Michigan, Spring Hill Assembly in Tennessee, and Fairfax Assembly in Kansas. GM says those projects will push its U.S. production above 2 million vehicles a year once they’re fully running.

The 2027 TAG XL Lite Teardrop Debuts as a Nice Update from Tent Camping
9 photos
Photo: nuCamp
Not all good things happen with a bang and a lot of fanfare, believe it or not. nuCamp RV, one of the most appreciated U.S. manufacturers of light and compact towables, is choosing a stealth debut for what is bound to become a popular model as soon as the word spreads.
That would be the TAG XL Lite (also spelled as T@G), which debuts as a 2027 model and is, as its name says, the Lite version of the already popular TAG XL, itself a variation of the TAG model that debuted way back in 2013.
Designed to be an upgrade from traditional tent camping, the TAG XL Lite bets big on quality work, basic comfort, and the same unmistakable nuCamp aesthetics nuCamp customers and fans have come to love. At the base of this new floorplan is the old – and very popular – TAG SE .
The TAG and sister TAB series of teardrop travel trailers from nuCamp are widely regarded as the best you're going to find right now. Never too big or heavy as to become a real hassle to maneuver and own, yet spacious enough to fit a variable range of creature comforts, they promise lifetime use and enjoyment thanks to their zero-wood construction and Amish-built quality cabinetry.
Photo: nuCamp They're not fussy or overly complicated, and that's by design. The same goes for the latest addition to the family, the TAG XL Lite.
This one is a rolling contradiction, if you think about it. It's an XL version of the standard TAG model, yet now it's Lite(r), so it's big and pared down at the same time. That, too, is intentional because nuCamp imagines it as an update from traditional tent camping, but with the extra body width of the TAG XL, so it's a step-up from a traditional teardrop trailer as well.
Construction is the same as with all the other TAGs, so you have a composite, wood-free structure on a Lippert-built frame, with an aluminum framework and an exterior layer of fiberglass. The trailer rides on a single axle with Dexter spring suspension, electric brakes, alloy wheels, and aggressive offroad tires, and you also get custom fenders like on its better equipped brother, the TAG XL.
Photo: nuCamp The layout is similar to the one on its predecessor, but pared down to earn the "Lite" moniker. This is a bigger teardrop with a tailgate that could be turned into a galley if you need one and have the extra cash, or you could spec it with the gear you already own, or use it as it is. That's what Lite is all about, the freedom to use it however you see fit.
Coming in at 13 feet 7 inches (4.1 meters) in overall length, the TAG XL Lite is 7 feet 11 inches (2.4 meters) wide and offers 49 inches (124.5 cm) of headroom inside. You obviously won't be able to stand up inside, but you can sit up without bumping your head and that's always a plus – especially with this one, which comes with a foldable mattress so you can have a dry, safe space you can retire to in case the weather turns.
Equipped as standard with two entry doors, the TAG XL Lite features storage at the head of the bed, while the foot of the bed allows for a pass-through connection to the rear storage space or tailgate galley. When nuCamp says they're building this teardrop to be basic, simple, and unfussy, that's exactly what they deliver.
Photo: nuCamp The TAG XL Lite comes with no exterior graphics and fewer windows than any other TAG, no holding tanks, no furnace, and no appliances in the tailgate, which nuCamp describes as "a highly versatile storage space."
It does, however, come equipped with a 6,000-BTU AC unit mounted in the partition between the foot of the bed and tailgate, a three-speed fan you can upgrade to a MaxxAir fan for better ventilation inside, and two opening windows that have a slight tint and integrated privacy blinds and flyscreens.
Also standard is premium soft-close cabinetry hand-built in the Amish community in Ohio, LED lights, an exterior solar port you can use for a briefcase-style solar panel, and power outlets and USB charging points. There isn't much of any of these to go around, because the trailer itself is very compact – again, by design .
Photo: nuCamp Options include three colors to choose from for the roof and sidewalls and add-ons like a 26-liter (0.9 cu-ft) 12V Bluetooth cooler that would sit in the tailgate, the tri-fold multifunctional mattress that's both bed and lounge, an unmounted steel spare tire, a rear receiver with a 150-lb (68-kg) capacity, and the aforementioned MaxxAir fan.
The 2026 TAG XL Lite has a gross weight rating of 2,200 lbs (998 kg), with an empty weight of just 990 lbs (449 kg) and a tongue weight of just 76 lbs (34.5 kg).
Photo: nuCamp MSRP is at a hair under $20,000, but sale prices will vary according to options (if any) and dealer location. While nuCamp hasn't made much fuss about the new floorplan, failing to even feature a video tour on their socials, they do have a short walkthrough on the official page .

A Tesla Semi caught fire on Interstate 880 in Hayward, California, on Tuesday evening, and there was no crash. The electric truck’s lithium-ion battery burned long enough to keep the southbound freeway closed for about 10 hours.
The driver got out unhurt. But a Class 8 electric truck catching fire on its own, in traffic, is something Tesla and its growing list of Semi customers need to explain.
What happened on I-880
The fire broke out at around 5:35 p.m. PT in the southbound lanes near Route 92. CHP Hayward then closed I-880 in both directions, citing “the potential risk of hazardous chemical smoke,” and posted these photos from the scene:
🚨 TRAFFIC ALERT – I-880 FULL CLOSURE 🚨 A Tesla semi-truck has caught fire on I-880, resulting in a complete shutdown of both northbound and southbound lanes due to the potential risk of hazardous chemical smoke. pic.twitter.com/O01z32nxpZ — CHP Hayward (@CHPHayward) October 28, 2026
The driver told officers the truck caught fire and that they didn’t know why. No other vehicles were involved.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Northbound reopened Tuesday night. Southbound took much longer. CHP initially warned that the battery could burn for 15 to 18 hours, but crews beat that estimate, and CHP Hayward posted that all lanes were open at around 3:30 a.m. Wednesday.
The CHP photos show firefighters laying foam around the burned-out tractor, with the front of a Premier Trailer Leasing trailer charred behind it. The truck’s operator hasn’t been identified, and Tesla, which doesn’t have a press office, hasn’t commented. The cause is under investigation.
The second Semi fire to close a California interstate
We’ve been here before. In August 2024, a Tesla-operated Semi caught fire on I-80 near Emigrant Gap while driving from Livermore to Tesla’s facility in Sparks, Nevada. At the time, no crash was reported. The NTSB later found the truck had left the road on a curve, hit a delineator post and a tree, and its battery ignited after the impact. Firefighters used about 50,000 gallons of water, and the lanes stayed closed for up to 15 hours.
Hayward is different. Without a crash, the focus shifts to the truck itself: the battery pack, the high-voltage system, the drive units, or something as ordinary as a tire or brake fire that spread.
And the timing isn’t great for Tesla. The company only started volume production of the Semi in Nevada this year, after nearly a decade of delays. WattEV ordered 370 Semis in May, mostly for drayage at the Port of Oakland, just a few miles up I-880 from where Tuesday’s truck burned. In September, Tesla was also named lead supplier on a 2,500-truck ZET SCALE order.
Electrek’s Take
First, some perspective, because this fire is going to get used as an anti-EV talking point. Truck fires are common. According to NFPA data , US fire departments responded to an average of 15,462 large-truck fires per year between 2018 and 2022. That’s about 42 a day, in a fleet that’s overwhelmingly diesel. Mechanical failure was a factor in 44% of them, and only about 2% were tied to a collision.
The same goes for cars. NFPA and DOT data put the US average at one vehicle fire for every 17 million miles traveled, and combustion vehicles make up the vast majority of that fleet. Tesla claims one fire per 140 million miles for its own vehicles. That’s Tesla’s number, but independent data, like government figures we’ve covered before , points the same way: gas vehicles catch fire more often than EVs.

Photo: Bring a Trailer/autoevolution
Had to do a bit of math for this one, but according to the numbers, the value on this car went up by just over $61 for every mile that it’s been driven. And it hasn’t been driven that much. The original owner put just 799 miles on the odometer before deciding to auction it off.
The car retailed for $134,080 back when SRT was its own brand, and just yesterday it sold for a whopping $183,000. The value shot up by 36.5% on a car that sold rather poorly, originally. You guys remember how much Dodge/SRT struggled with fifth-gen Viper sales, right? Sales were so poor that production had to be cut and paused, at one point.
Overall, the fifth-gen Viper was by far the lowest-selling generation in the nameplate’s history, which led directly to its discontinuation. This had such an effect on Dodge that they never even considered coming up with an all-new model. I guess when you’re doing so well with your Hellcat-powered Challengers and Chargers, you’d rather not rock the boat too much.
But now that we’ve entered the era of electrification, I can totally see the Viper coming back in whatever capacity. Personally, I think there’s a place for it in the combustion engine supercar segment, but an EV would work too, I guess – it’s better than nothing. Ideally though, I’d like to see an all-new Viper taking the fight to the C8 Corvette . That would be spectacular.
And yes, they should go ahead and make it rear mid-engined. It worked for the Corvette and it should work for the Viper too. That’s the category supercars need to attack nowadays. Otherwise, who are you going to challenge with a front-engine supercar? The 12Cilindri and the Vanquish? The AMG-GT? I think not.
In terms of specs, aside from its Gunmetal Pearl colorway, this Viper GTS also comes with dual black racing stripes, xenon headlights, a GTS-specific vented hood, a rearview camera, integrated rear spoiler, dual side exhaust outlets, plus a set of black 18” and 19” Venom alloy wheels rocking staggered-width Pirelli P Zero rubber and red Viper-branded Brembo calipers over vented rotors.
Photo: Bring a Trailer Interior highlights include the black Nappa leather and Alcantara Sabelt bucket seats, a 12-speaker sound system, power-adjustable pedals, automatic climate control, cruise control, sat-nav, and a leather-wrapped steering wheel.
As for the engine, it’s a massive… and I do mean massive 8.4-liter V10 of the hand-assembled variety, pushing out 640 horsepower and 600 lb-ft of torque. Everything gets sent to the rear wheels via a Tremec six-speed manual gearbox.
Getting all that power down can be a struggle, but if you hook properly, you should be able to hit 60 mph (97 kph) from a standstill in about 3.5 seconds. Meanwhile, the top speed is 206 mph (332 kph).

By Gavin van Marle
28 October 2026
After recently passing 15m teu, the global orderbook for containership newbuildings could near 16m teu by the end of the year, according to new analysis from Alphaliner.
“Before the end of the year, another 40 or so ‘megamax’ newbuilding contracts from Maersk, Yang Ming [both expected soon], CMA CGM, and MSC [both believed signed, but yet to be confirmed by Alphaliner] will push the global newbuilding pipeline very close to 16m teu in the last quarter of 2026,” it writes today.
On the Maersk order, Alphaliner reports that the carrier is exclusively talking to Chinese yards on cost and building slot availability.
It added: “Reportedly, the carrier is looking to place firm orders for 12 ships of 24,000 teu, potentially with options attached for a second series of 12.
“Tonnage of this category would currently be priced at around $240m per vessel.”
Meanwhile, according to analysts at Drewry, the global fleet currently totals 34m teu, which means that, even without the unconfirmed 40 newbuildings noted by Alphaliner, the orderbook represents 45% of the current fleet.
Almost a third of this – 4.9m teu – has been ordered this year alone, and should orders for the extra 40 vessels be confirmed, this would be likely well over 5.5m teu and make it a record year in terms of newbuildings ordered, beating last year’s 5.4m teu.
However, shippers hoping the influx of new capacity will lead to a sudden collapse in freight rates may be disappointed, according to Vespucci Maritime chief executive Lars Jensen, who spoke at a Hapag-Lloyd press briefing a few days ago.
“The market is not going to drop off a cliff. When we talk about the market crashing, that would be like what we saw in the financial crisis back in 2008. That, for sure, is not what we’re looking at,” he said.
“How I would more likely characterise the coming years is as a regular run-of-the-mill cyclical downturn. This is a cyclical industry, it has been ever since it was born, and this is another one of those cycles.
“So a crash? Absolutely not. But do we have too much capacity compared to what we can absorb? Yes, that is also the case,” he added.
Meanwhile, Hapag-Lloyd CEO Rolf Habben Jansen added that the growing imbalance of the main container trades – particularly the yawning chasm between China’s export and import volumes – as well as an expected increase in vessels sent to be scrapped, would mitigate against new capacity.
“Of course, the orderbook is bigger than it has ever been, but there are a couple of things to keep in mind – one is that the current fleet is aging, so we will start to see scrapping going up.
“We can debate about when and at what pace, but that’s definitely going to come up,” he said.
“There’s the growth, especially the growth on some of those dominant legs – when you look at the middle of 2023 until now, the growth on the dominant legs has been about 25%, which is unbelievable.
“If you combine that with some of the inefficiencies we see popping up because of trade barriers and tariffs, one cannot rule out that we’re going to see another couple of years of pretty decent growth,” he said.
Mr Habben Jansen also pointed out that lead times for newbuildings had lengthened to near historic highs as slots as shipyards have become increasingly full.
“If you look at the orderbook today, where traditionally it used to cover two, or two and a half years of deliveries, nowadays it’s more like four, or four and a half years.
“If you order a ship today, you will only get it by 2030,” he added.

The FDA has outlined a process for allowing a single application to cover multiple variants of a gene therapy. At the same time, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services has revealed plans to expand the Cell and Gene Therapy Access Model to increase patient access to these products.
The FDA is full speed ahead with efforts to accelerate the development of and access to personalized gene therapies for rare diseases, issuing new draft guidance on Tuesday afternoon to help usher drug developers through the approval process for these medicines.
The draft guidance —a full court press from the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) that includes the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) in addition to FDA—seeks to provide “a clear and scientifically rigorous framework for BLA submission and postapproval management” of these therapies, Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research (CBER) Director Karim Mikhail said in a prepared statement on Tuesday. “We are helping to ensure that patients—including those with ultra-rare conditions for whom no treatment currently exists—can more efficiently access therapies that may be life-changing.”
Key to the guidance is the Individualized Feature Space (IFS), a set of pre-defined criteria describing how a gene therapy product can vary between patients—say, those whose disease is caused by a different genetic mutation—while still remaining within the scope of a single biologics license application (BLA).
“When a new patient-specific variant of the therapy falls within those boundaries and assays show that the variant has adequate safety and activity, sponsors can submit it to the BLA without needing to perform additional clinical trials,” the FDA and CMS said in the joint release.
The guidance offers clarity on how sponsors can structure a BLA capable of accommodating “multiple patient-specific product variants,” and how new variants can be efficiently added after approval to avoid additional trials.
The document also addresses other issues of concern in the gene therapy space, including manufacturing, safety testing and labeling.
Tuesday’s draft guidance follows similar initiatives, including the FDA’s Plausible Mechanism Pathway , announced by former Commissioner Marty Makary and former CBER director Vinay Prasad in November last year. The pathway was intended to expedite therapies for diseases that affect an exceedingly small patient population, for which randomized trials are not feasible.
In an article published in The New England Journal of Medicine on Nov. 13, 2025, Makary and Prasad highlighted the case of Baby KJ , a young child with an ultrarare genetic condition called CPS1 deficiency who was treated with a single-use CRISPR therapy that was produced specifically for him, as an example of the pathway’s intentions.
The latest draft guidance also comes less than two weeks after the FDA debuted its new Rare Disease Framework Initiative , intended to standardize the agency’s approach to scientific evidence and bring rare disease therapies to patients faster.

CMS also made its intentions and commitment to increasing access to the often-pricey therapies clear.
“A medical breakthrough only matters to patients if they can get it,” CMS Administrator Mehmet Oz said in Tuesday’s press release, adding that CMS is “bringing state Medicaid programs together to negotiate with drug manufacturers to help put life-changing therapies within reach.”
In January 2024, CMS introduced the Cell and Gene Therapy (CGT) Access Model , a voluntary initiative whereby CMS negotiates voluntary outcomes-based agreements on behalf of state Medicaid programs for cell and gene therapies to increase patient access to these products. The model initially focused on gene therapies for sickle cell disease. In December that year, Vertex Pharmaceuticals and bluebird bio —the developers of Casgevy and Lyfgenia, respectively—joined the program.
On Tuesday, CMS said it would take steps to broaden this model beyond sickle cell disease.
“In the coming months, CMS will release a Request for Applications (RFA) for manufacturers designed to broaden the model’s scope and enable negotiations to begin sooner after a therapy receives FDA approval or licensure, while also welcoming applications for therapies already approved or licensed,” the agency said.
The FDA’s and CMS’ most recent action also coincides with the National Organization for Rare Diseases Breakthrough Summit in Washington, D.C., which has included presentations from Mikhail and his CDER counterpart Michael Davis.
RBC Capital Markets analysts, who were attending the summit, expressed optimism about recent regulatory efforts in the rare disease space.
“Ultimately, we came away incrementally more positive on the rare disease regulatory setup, with both Mikhail and Davis striking a notably constructive tone around the newly launched Rare Disease Framework Initiative and a strong desire to harmonize regulatory standards across the two divisions in order to ultimately increase predictability for sponsors,” they wrote in a note to investors on Wednesday.
With the U.S. midterm elections less than a week away, the analysts said that multiple congressional staffers “expressed bipartisan support for clinical trial reform for rare disease.”

NASCAR 26 Review (PS5): Make Another Left Turn!
40 photos
Photo: autoevolution
When Ken Block released the first Gymkhana video over a decade and a half ago, it captivated millions of people worldwide. We hadn’t seen anything quite like it until then. The series peaked at one point, and then started going downhill from there. You can observe this phenomenon in many aspects of life.
Driving a 200-hp car at the track for the first time will feel exhilarating. Using the same vehicle at the same venue for years in a row can become repetitive and boring as you get used to the acceleration, braking and G-Forces. So either start upgrading or at least go drive on a different track entirely to keep things exciting.
I’ve seen so many racing/automotive clips online over the past 20 years that I will rarely truly enjoy seeing a new one in 2026. It does happen a few times each year, though, and the latest Repco Supercars highlights video from the Gold Coast 500 is a good example of that. Those guys are godlike in the way they’re pushing their cars to the limit, and the excitement is rarely unmatched by other series.
Of course, there plenty of options out there, and different people will have different preferences. Rallying has really gotten under my skin recently, as has endurance racing. Drifting and time attack have been my favorites for many years. But I’ve also long abandoned drag racing as it felt downright boring to me. I’m aware of its complexity, but that does nothing to keep me invested in watching.
And the same goes for oval racing. I wasn’t particularly thrilled at the thought of testing the new NASCAR 26 game, especially since last year’s release wasn’t nearly impressive enough. It was forgettable at best, and I feared the worst for the latest iteration.
We didn’t need another podcast Photo: autoevolution The game starts of with Lynyrd Skynyrd’s Sweet Home Alabama playing in the background, which felt like a good choice for this type of racing. As for the actual intro, I couldn’t really tell if it was exactly the same like last year which immediately made me think this could easily be a rinse-and-repeat type of job.
Going into my first race further amplified that sensation, as I struggled to figure out if anything had truly changed from the previous title. Switching to Career mode, there was that same Dale Earnhardt Jr. podcast again that I couldn’t skip. There are many platforms out there where you can listen to a podcast if you want to, but I imagine anyone who purchases a video game like this is more interested in the driving part.
Choosing the Team Color is a simple feature, but I enjoyed how simple it ease to select a theme you like and move on. I started in the ARCA Menard series, and Jamie McMurray insisted on taking me out for a Drafting lesson before the first race at Daytona. As I got up to 178 mph (286 kph), I once again realized there’s no true sense of speed in this game which is highly disappointing.
Playing on the easiest mode available, I had no trouble getting P1 in both the practice and the qualifying sessions, while Cleetus McFarland ’s virtual replica was down in P6. I’m not sure why I was only allowed to do one lap in qualifying, though. It might be standard practice in NASCAR, but it’s not something I’m used to.
Use a steering wheel Photo: autoevolution Going into the race, it was only fun for half a lap as that’s all it took for me to get ahead of everyone else and not have to worry about them again. The spotter will keep you updated on the situation around you, but it feels like a highly-artificial experience which might sound redundant given this is a videogame.
Using the PS5 controller to steer the car is by no means ideal, as it was almost impossible for me to stay on the right lines or get high up on the bank close to the walls. I realize you can set it all up for a better experience, but I could only think about how easy it is to be precise in Gran Turismo 7 using the controller’s motion sensor.
I also suddenly found myself becoming irate at the idea that there has to be a dedicated game for each type of racing, which only seems to serve one purpose (and it’s not customer satisfaction). Anyway, racing in the afternoon the lighting and the track looked great, but I can’t say the same thing about the replay: in here, the graphics mostly looked ancient in comparison to both GT7 and either one of the two modern Assetto Corsa titles.
Also, there was no chance for me to get some nice shots of the action with no photo mode available. Is something like that really that hard to implement? I decided to move on and see what a quick race at Watkins Glen would be like, using a truck this time. I’ve never been so happy about finally getting to use the brakes!
What year is it? Photo: autoevolution Going around in circles, constantly on the rev-limiter in top gear lap in and lap out almost reminds me of driving a car equipped with a CVT gearbox if that makes sense. I think I remember reading that the developers improved the tire model for NASCAR 26, and I was surprised to see (and hear) I could lock up the brakes going into Turn One.
There’s a vague, artificial sensation about it, and I soon discovered I would lock the brakes on every single occasion regardless of how careful I was. Even so, it wasn’t like they had a massive impact on the situation, as I could still safely navigate through every corner ahead. I kept thinking I was playing a game from the late ‘90s, with slightly better graphics than what we had available at the time.
NASCAR 26 would have been a decent experience then, but it just can’t stack up to the competition today. And no, saying that there are no better NASCAR games out there doesn’t absolve it of its flaws. I even switched to Expert mode in an attempt to improve my experience with the game, and I might have enjoyed driving at 185 mph (297 kph) for a minute or two.
The car’s sound doesn’t bounce off the walls as nicely as it does in AC EVO and I once again found myself eager to see what else I could do to have some fun. The Peak Performance part of the game might deliver on that, especially if you’re keen on getting educated on the topic. You’ll go through six different episodes that will teach you a thing or two about how you should tackle different situations and corners.
Photo: autoevolution I felt confused hearing the lyrics to “ Dale Earnhardt ”, a song by The Hot Skillet Lickers. Isn’t it a bit biased to include it in the soundtrack? Am I nitpicking over tiny details here? I mean, if Keiichi Tsuchiya worked on developing a game focused on drifting, and the soundtrack featured a song praising him as the all-time greatest, I would have had the exact same reaction.
Conclusion It’s been 12 months since I played NASCAR 25 and it was certainly a forgettable experience. So if I couldn’t really tell if NASCAR 26 was any better or at least different, what does that have to say about the new game? Also, picture this: the NASCAR 26 Gold Edition is available on the Xbox Series X|S, PS5 and Steam and costs 80,99€ (roughly $90).
If you want a more realistic driving experience that includes both tarmac and off-road driving, I’d suggest the Assetto Corsa Evo and Rally bundle instead (it’s typically less than $80 but even has a 20% discount these days).
Photo: autoevolution If you want a huge selection of cars, and at least 500 hours of game play worth of your money, go for Gran Turismo 7 – it’s 70$ but could be even cheaper by Christmas. If you insist on choosing NASCAR, last year’s game now costs less than $50 on STEAM and I still think it’s severely overpriced.
But hey, maybe I just don’t get it and I’m too fond of other racing genres to objectively assess the situation. Oh, and I’m giving this game a lower score than last year just because of how annoyed I am with companies pretending it’s OK to charge this much for this small of a change year in and year out. End of rant.
Rating: 55/100

KYIV, Ukraine — American diesel prices rose for a second straight week as Russia’s seaborne crude exports reached their highest weekly value since the country launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine. The price hike comes weeks after U.S. President Donald Trump moved to ease restrictions on Russian diesel and pressure Kyiv to spare Russian refineries ahead of the U.S. midterm elections.
Diesel averaged $6.35 a gallon on Monday, just below the record $6.53 set in September, according to data from the U.S. Energy Information Administration .
The economy is the top issue heading into the Nov. 3 midterms, with 84% of registered voters calling it “very important” to their vote and 54% saying the same of energy policy, according to a Pew Research Center survey conducted Sept. 28 to Oct. 4.
“The president decided to pin this problem not on Putin, but on me. Explaining to his people that because of this, diesel prices in America are going up. That is completely untrue,” Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said of Trump’s recent claims that Ukraine’s attacks on Russian refineries were to blame for the price increases.
Trends in federal data back up the Ukrainian president, showing that the steep initial rise in diesel prices followed the start of the Iran war — not Ukrainian strikes on Russian production infrastructure.
U.S. diesel stayed below $3.90 a gallon from August 2025 until the U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran began Feb. 28, then jumped nearly 25% in a week to $4.86, according to the Energy Information Administration.
“This crisis has its roots in the Middle East. Everyone understands that perfectly well. Everyone knows how to do the math,” Zelenskyy said on Oct. 12, quoting his remarks to the Warsaw Security Forum. “If Russia accounts for 2.2% of global diesel supplies, what impact can it have on the price? That’s how negligible it is.”
Even Moscow’s senior officials agree.
“The key guarantee of full stabilization of this market is the speediest normalization of the situation around the Persian Gulf, overcoming the conflict around Iran,” Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Georgy Borisenko told reporters Oct. 12.
The International Energy Agency confirmed in an Oct. 14 report that easing Russia’s diesel export ban is unlikely to materially change global supplies because Russia lacks the working refinery capacity.
Critics of the deal
The diesel sales will barely move American prices before the vote, but the deal would benefit Russia disproportionately and cost Kyiv one of its few levers against the Kremlin, according to the Institute for the Study of War and the Carnegie Russia Eurasia Center .
The current situation gives Moscow deeper diplomatic ties with Washington — economic cooperation that continues despite Russia’s attacks on Ukraine’s more vulnerable energy grid — as well as more money for its war chest and the prospect that U.S. pressure will halt Ukraine’s strikes on its refineries that help fund the war, experts at both institutions said.
“The diesel agreement gives Putin an opportunity to advance economic cooperation with Washington before any settlement in Ukraine,” Carnegie senior fellow Tatiana Stanovaya wrote on Oct. 14. “Economic agreements can coexist with unchanged demands on Ukraine and continued military pressure.”
The Kremlin is also using the deal to win U.S. support for its negotiating position with Ukraine, part of a recurring effort to offer Washington economic incentives it claims are unrelated to the war “in order to extract concessions from the U.S. regarding the war,” ISW said.
Agioi Fanendes, a Malta-flagged medium-sized tanker, transits the Bosphorus in Istanbul, Turkey, April 11, 2024. The tanker, loaded with diesel fuel, departed Russia on Friday, Oct. 23, 2026, headed for the United States. (Yoruk Isik/Reuters)
Critics in Kyiv and Washington, including members of Trump’s own party, warn the deal will put more oil money in Russian hands and disproportionately impact Ukraine. Zelenskyy told the Warsaw Security Forum that the country has “just one oil refinery,” while Russia has 32 major refineries, according to the International Energy Agency.
Four Republican and three Democratic senators urged the Trump administration Oct. 11 to “immediately reverse course,” saying in a joint statement that “the United States should not provide Putin with a financial lifeline while Russia continues to kill Ukrainian civilians.”
Two days later, 12 senators from both parties, including Republicans Mitch McConnell, R-Ky., and John Cornyn, R-Texas, wrote to Trump in a letter that the deal will have “a negligible impact on fuel prices” and “is a gift to our adversary and a betrayal of our Allies.”
“Putin is looking for a way to get the United States to pressure Ukraine to stop striking those refineries,” Rep. Don Bacon, R-Neb., wrote the day the deal was announced.
Not enough to offset losses
Ukraine’s strikes have taken some Russian diesel off the market.
Russian diesel production fell by nearly 30% as attacks on refineries intensified, the International Energy Agency said in a Sept. 17 analysis .
The estimated gross value of Russia’s seaborne crude shipments hit a wartime high of $2.76 billion this week, up roughly $430 million from the week before, Bloomberg reported.
No strikes on Russian refineries were reported last week, and the lull has allowed Moscow to boost processing rates, likely diverting crude that would otherwise have been exported, the outlet reported.
But the Gulf’s losses are far larger. Diesel exports from the region dropped to 390,000 barrels a day in August, just over a quarter of prewar levels, according to International Energy Agency figures .
Russia’s promised deliveries won’t close that gap.
The first shipment equals just about 2% of U.S. diesel demand over a month, CNBC reported. Goldman Sachs estimated the first two months of deliveries would cut wholesale prices on the U.S. Gulf Coast by just $1 to $2 a barrel, or roughly 2 to 5 cents a gallon.
“Now we can see how cash will start flowing back into Russia through the diesel deal,” Zelenskyy told reporters at a European Union summit in Brussels on Oct. 16, according to Reuters .
“This diesel deal will never be enough to offset the impact of the Strait of Hormuz on global markets. But it will put more money straight into Putin’s pocket to fund this war.”
Trump eased sanctions on Russian diesel after an Oct. 9 call with Russian President Vladimir Putin, saying in a Truth Social post that Russia would supply hundreds of thousands of tons of diesel fuel “immediately” and that diesel prices would come down “IN RECORD NUMBERS, AND FAST!”
The same day, U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner told Ukrainian negotiators in Miami that the White House hoped the diesel deal would soften Moscow’s stance on peace talks. Witkoff met Putin for in-person negotiations last week for the ninth time since February 2025.
Kyiv offered to refrain from striking Russian refineries if Moscow stopped hitting Ukraine’s energy infrastructure, Zelenskyy said Oct. 11.
The current price of diesel fuel is displayed at a gas station in Encinitas, California, on Oct. 21, 2026. (Mike Blake/Reuters)
Ukraine paused refinery strikes at Trump’s request, but Russia kept hitting Ukraine’s energy infrastructure, prompting Kyiv to resume its own counterattacks, Zelenskyy told the Financial Times on Oct. 15.
“We’re done,” he said.
Within days of Trump’s sanction announcement, Ukrainian officials accused Washington of pressuring Kyiv to capitulate by withholding missile warnings and throttling the military’s essential Starlink connectivity , intelligence that Zelenskyy said “helps save people’s lives.”
Trump denied any interruption in missile warnings or Starlink service, but Ukrainian officials have stood by their account, prompting Zelenskyy to say he felt betrayed by the U.S.
Both have since been restored, Zelenskyy said Saturday, but Russia’s attacks have not let up.
Russia fired 16 ballistic missiles and more than 280 drones at Ukraine overnight Monday into Tuesday, targeting “energy, logistics and ordinary urban infrastructure” almost everywhere, Zelenskyy said .
The barrage came as the U.N. Independent International Commission of Inquiry on Ukraine concluded that Russian authorities had committed war crimes and crimes against humanity through attacks on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure.

2027 Ford LMDh Hypercar Spotted at Monza, Coyote V8 Screams
10 photos
Photo: NM2255 | Raw Car Sounds/YouTube
Back in early 2025, Ford revealed that it plans to return to top-tier endurance racing with an LMDh race car. The hypercar is set to join the 2027 season of the FIA World Endurance Championship. The prototype has yet to get an official unveiling, but it's been spotted testing at the Monza circuit , in Italy.
The LMDh race car was first seen at the Paul Ricard circuit in France back in August. Ford also ran tests at the Portimão circuit in Portugal and at Silverstone. At Monza, the company began using a second chassis (though only one is captured in the video below).
Ford has yet to name its endurance racer, but we do know it's being developed in collaboration with Oreca, which provides the chassis. The vehicle features a naturally-aspirated 5.4-liter V8 engine derived from the Coyote. The mill was fitted onto the chassis and fired up for the first time in July 2026 . The hybrid system delivers 680 horsepower.
As seen in previous testing sessions, the car featured a blue-and-white camouflage-style design. Apart from a few details unique to this car (like the headlamps, for instance), Ford's LMDh racer looks very familiar. It has the typical canopy-style center section, a high center fin, a massive rear wing, and a heavily contoured front splitter and rear diffuser.
Ford's new hypercar will mark the company's return to top-tier endurance racing after several decades. Ford's last effort (that also included racing at Le Mans) dates all the way back to 1969. That's when the GT40 won the 24 Hours of Le Mans for the fourth consecutive year.
Ford has campaigned a race car based on the modern GT in recent years. A factory-backed effort joined the World Endurance Championship in the LM GTE-Pro, scoring a class win at the 2016 24 Hours of Le Mans.
Ford's yet-unnamed prototype is one of two LMDh race cars that will join the 2027 season. The other one is the McLaren MCL-HY. Unlike the Ford hypercar, the McLaren uses a chassis developed by Dallara.
The 2027 FIA WEC season will include nine events, with the 6 Hours of Silverstone returning to the calendar for the first time since 2019. The championship will commence in March in Qatar and will conclude in November in Bahrain. The 24 Hours of Le Mans race is scheduled on June 12-13.
The hypercar class will see no fewer than nine automakers battle for supremacy. Ford and McLaren will join Aston Martin, Toyota, Cadillac, BMW, Genesis, Ferrari, and Peugeot. Alpine will not return for the 2027 season.
Ford Racing will fully reveal its 2027 hypercar in late November. Until that happens, hit the play button below to see it doing quick laps around Monza. Make sure you crank up the volume to hear the Coyote V8 engine scream.

JACKSONVILLE, Fla. — The Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration has removed more than 10,000 commercial driver training providers from its federal registry since December 2025 and more than 100 noncompliant electronic logging devices from its approved list, according to the agency’s chief safety officer.
Steve Dowling outlined the agency’s expanding enforcement efforts Wednesday during a keynote address at the second annual WEX OTR Summit in Jacksonville, Florida, saying FMCSA is strengthening oversight of commercial driver training, licensing, carrier registration and trucking operations.
Dowling, who became FMCSA’s chief safety officer in August, said the agency is taking a more comprehensive approach to identifying unsafe trucking companies and preventing fraud before carriers enter the industry.
“If we want to protect the industry, we need to make sure that we start at the driver level and how they’re trained,” Dowling told attendees.
The former California Highway Patrol official and Covenant Logistics safety executive said FMCSA’s enforcement strategy focuses on five stages of commercial motor vehicle operations: training, licensing, registration, operations and enforcement.
More than 10,000 training providers removed
Dowling said more than 10,000 providers have been removed from FMCSA’s Training Provider Registry since December 2025.
The figure represents the agency’s broader registry cleanup and should not be confused with the separate emergency enforcement action announced in August.
That action targeted approximately 110 commercial driver training schools whose operations were linked to more than 5,000 drivers cited for English-language proficiency violations, according to Dowling.
“Since December of ’25, there have been more than 10,000 providers that have been removed from the training provider registry,” Dowling said.
He said the agency intends to continue reviewing driver training programs to ensure schools meet federal requirements.
“You’ve seen a real increased enforcement effort from us and emphasis on that,” Dowling said. “You’re going to continue to see us try to make sure that the schools are doing what they’re supposed to do.”
FMCSA is also strengthening oversight of state commercial driver’s license programs and third-party testing operations.
Dowling said the agency wants trucking companies to have confidence that drivers who receive CDLs have met consistent federal standards, regardless of the state issuing the license.
ELD crackdown expands
FMCSA has also intensified its scrutiny of electronic logging devices , which are used to record commercial drivers’ hours of service .
Dowling said the agency has removed more than 100 noncompliant devices from its registered ELD list and prevented nearly 600 others from being approved.
“We’ve removed over 100 noncompliant ELDs from the registered device list, and we’ve prevented nearly 600 from making it onto the list entirely,” Dowling said.
He said the agency is particularly concerned about logging systems that can be manipulated to conceal hours-of-service violations.
“You can’t go in and edit logs by making a phone call,” Dowling said. “Anytime we hear of that, we’re going and investigating.”
Dowling encouraged motor carriers to verify that their ELD providers remain on FMCSA’s registered device list and that the systems they use cannot be improperly manipulated.
He said the agency intends to continue strengthening oversight of ELD manufacturers and other transportation technology providers.
FMCSA targets chameleon carriers through registration overhaul
Another major enforcement priority is identifying so-called chameleon carriers — trucking companies that shut down and reopen under new identities to evade safety enforcement, penalties or other regulatory requirements.
Dowling said FMCSA’s modernized registration system, Motus, is designed to improve verification of carrier ownership and principal places of business.
He described instances in which multiple trucking companies have registered using the same address or post office box, potentially indicating attempts to conceal common ownership or circumvent federal requirements.
“One location that maybe has 20 different DOT numbers coming out of a PO box in a location, that’s a problem,” Dowling said.
The new registration platform is intended to identify suspicious applications before federal operating authority is granted.
Dowling acknowledged that Motus has experienced technical problems during its rollout.
He said approximately 95% of carrier registration activity was functioning through the system based on data he reviewed the previous week, but acknowledged that problems affecting the remaining users were unacceptable.
“That’s not acceptable to us,” Dowling said of the difficulties experienced by some applicants.
He said FMCSA temporarily suspended its biennial registration update requirement while the agency works to address technical issues.
Dowling said the registration changes are helping prevent potentially fraudulent businesses from entering the trucking industry.
“There are thousands of people that we’re keeping out of the industry because we’ve initiated [Motus],” Dowling said.
He did not provide a precise count of blocked applicants or a breakdown of how many were suspected of fraud rather than affected by registration problems.
Federal investigators coordinate on trucking fraud
During a question-and-answer session following the keynote, Dowling said FMCSA is increasingly working with the Justice Department, FBI and federal prosecutors to investigate chameleon carriers and other suspected trucking fraud.
He said some investigations involve networks of companies that operate across multiple jurisdictions, making it necessary to coordinate with other law enforcement agencies.
“You’re going to see cases that start coming out that are specifically combating against chameleon carriers,” Dowling said.
He said investigators are looking beyond individual violations to identify connections among companies, owners, equipment and other operations.
“These investigations usually aren’t just linear to where, okay, it’s one violation to one carrier,” Dowling said.
The agency is also relying on information provided by trucking companies, industry representatives and others who identify suspicious carriers or potentially noncompliant ELD providers.
Dowling said FMCSA is actively investigating those reports.
CDL enforcement effectiveness remains under review
Dowling also addressed questions about federal enforcement of non-domiciled CDLs and English-language proficiency requirements.
He said FMCSA is seeing indications that drivers who do not meet non-domiciled CDL requirements may also have English-language proficiency violations.
However, he acknowledged that the agency needs additional time and data to determine whether its enforcement initiatives are producing measurable reductions in crashes.
“Sometimes you have to be patient to be able to see if the things that you are doing works,” Dowling said.
He said FMCSA is collecting more information and examining connections among driver training, licensing records and crash investigations.
The agency is also working with state licensing authorities to ensure non-domiciled CDLs are issued and maintained in accordance with federal requirements.
Asked whether FMCSA has an accurate count of non-domiciled CDL holders currently operating in the United States, Dowling said he could not recall a specific figure.
He noted that some non-domiciled CDL holders remain legally eligible to operate and that the total number is changing as states implement federal restrictions.
Dowling said the agency is focusing on auditing state licensing processes rather than relying solely on a nationwide count.
Hours-of-service flexibility and safety scoring changes ahead
Looking ahead to 2027, Dowling said FMCSA is evaluating potential changes to hours-of-service regulations and its Safety Measurement System, which helps identify motor carriers for intervention.
He referenced ongoing research into additional hours-of-service flexibility, including sleeper-berth provisions and the 14-hour duty window.
Dowling said the agency wants to determine whether existing regulations can be adjusted without compromising efforts to prevent driver fatigue.
“Just because that’s what the rule is doesn’t mean we don’t need to look at it,” he said.
FMCSA is also examining how it uses inspection, crash and compliance data to identify high-risk motor carriers.
Dowling said the agency wants to focus its limited enforcement resources on operations presenting the greatest safety risks rather than minor administrative violations.
“We can get more predictive by data analysis on who is more likely to crash,” he said.
Why it matters: FMCSA’s expanded scrutiny of CDL schools, licensing agencies, electronic logging devices and carrier registrations could significantly change how trucking companies enter the market, recruit drivers and demonstrate compliance heading into 2027.

This 2016 BMW X5 Was Over $70,000 New, Just Sold $10,850
17 photos
Photo: Cars&Bids
If you dream about buying a cool third-generation BMW X5 , then this is your sign, because the value of this model has started reaching new lows.
In fact, the pictured example initially retailed for $70,845, and as mentioned in the title, it recently changed hands on the used car market, fetching $10,850. Thus, it has lost almost $60,000 in roughly one decade.
You are looking at an xDrive35d BMW X5 from the 2016 model year, which means that it packs a 3.0-liter inline-six turbodiesel under the hood. The N57 mill was good for 255 hp (258 ps/190 kW) and 413 pound-feet (560 Nm) of torque when the SUV was new, with the peak thrust available between 1,500 and 3,000 rpm, and the maximum output at 4,000 rpm.
Everything is channeled to the rear-biased xDrive all-wheel drive system through a smooth-shifting automatic transmission with eight forward gears. This model is clearly not a sprinter disguised as a premium mid-size SUV, but it took a very respectable 7+ seconds to push from 0-60 mph (0-97 kph), independent tests back in the day revealed, and had a 130 mph (210 kph) electronically limited top speed.
Other diesel versions included the xDrive40d and the M50d, with 309 hp (313 ps/230 kW) and 376 hp (381 ps/280 kW), respectively, as well as the xDrive30d, xDrive25d, and sDrive25d (RWD), which had 255 hp (258 ps/190 kW), 228 hp (231 ps/170 kW), and 215 hp (218 ps/160 kW), respectively. The lineup also included the sDrive and xDrive35i, xDrive40e, and xDrive50i, with 302 hp (306 ps/225 kW) for the former two, and 308 hp (313 ps/230 kW) and 444 hp (450 ps/331 kW) for the latter two, respectively.
Photo: Cars&Bids The X5 M sat at the top of the family, packing a 4.4-liter twin-turbocharged V8 engine with 567 hp (575 ps/423 kW) and 553 lb-ft (750 Nm) of torque, reaching 62 mph (100 kph) in 4.2 seconds. The X5 M Competition had 617 hp (625 ps/460 kW), and dropped the sprint time to 3.9 seconds. With the optional M Driver’s Pack, the X5 M hit 180 mph (290 kph).
This BMW X5 xDrive35d has a Mineral White Metallic paint finish and a Mocha interior. It features the M Sport Package, the Premium Package, Driver Assistance Package, Driver Assistance Plus Package, Cold Weather Package, Dakota leather upholstery, and a panoramic sunroof, the listing shows.
It has never been involved in an accident, but according to the seller, the rear bumper was replaced almost one year ago, after a car backed into its right rear corner. The usual chips and scratches and some dings on the outside, a crack in the left lower front bumper, curb rash on the wheels, weathered finish around the center caps, some corrosion on underbody hardware, wear on the seats and interior surfaces, and leaking front strut are the known flaws.
The BMW X5 in question had 120,900 miles (194,600 km) on the clock at the time of cataloging, so it is not exactly a low-mileage example. It had its four tires replaced in March 2025, and the engine oil and filter were changed in April 2024. Moreover, it also had its brakes serviced, coolant flushed, and intake manifold gasket replaced in October 2026, and the engine oil and filter changed in May 2026.
Photo: Cars&Bids Additional services entries were recorded in October 2025 and January 2025. In the former, the vehicle had its differential fluid, rear differential fluid, and transmission fluid flushed, the water pump and air filter replaced, the brakes serviced, and the engine oil and filter changed. And in the latter, it had its engine oil and filter changed, the brake fluid flushed, and the fuel filter and fuel tank module seal replaced.
Besides the vehicle , the new owner will get the factory all-weather floor and trunk mats, two keys, a front license plate mount, and the owner’s manuals. The seller says to have purchased this ride in February 2020, and they added some 44,200 miles (71,100 km) before parting ways with it for pennies on the dollar compared to the initial selling price.
But how much would an xDrive35d variant of the 2016 BMW X5 cost you in today’s used car market in the States? That would be between $11,500 and $16,500. Dealers could ask more, pushing the price into the $20,000 territory, and the trade-in value of this thing is said to be between $8,500 and $10,500. And for just under $11,000, the pictured machine is definitely a lot of car for the money.
Thus, all we can say is congrats to the buyer for scoring a great family hauler for basically nothing. The X5 in question was advertised on Cars&Bids, where the online auction ended on October 27, 2026. And if you want to see it in more detail, then you can do that here . However, before you head over to the listing, let us know if you would have bought this SUV for $10,850.

Forward Air has entered a two-year agreement to retain “a significant portion of the services currently provided” to a customer that it had previously indicated it might lose . Prior reports from Forward said the contract logistics customer accounted for 10% of its annual revenue, or roughly $250 million.
Under the agreement, the customer will continue using Forward ( NASDAQ: FWRD ) for certain services through 2028, according to a Wednesday news release. The deal allows the customer to transition some business away from Forward from November to March.
Revenue generated from the retained portion of the account has continued to grow this year and is expected to increase next year. Revenue in each remaining contract year (2026 to 2028) is expected to exceed the revenue generated by the account in 2025. No margin profile for the retained business was provided.
Forward initially said the customer was seeking to diversify its list of vendors, emphasizing that the customer’s potential departure had nothing to do with the service being provided. Forward said on its second-quarter call in August that it entered a non-binding agreement to save 50%, and potentially up to 75%, of the business.
“We are pleased to finalize this Agreement and believe it reflects the strength of our longstanding 20-year partnership and the exceptional service our team continues to provide,” said Shawn Stewart, Forward president and CEO. “By signing this Agreement, we should bring both greater visibility and predictability to our business and the associated profitability and resulting cash flow.”
Shares of FWRD were up 8.7% in premarket trading on Wednesday.

Tesla has started hiring in Vietnam, and one of its recruiters says the company is now “officially coming” to the country. The five open roles include a sales manager, a service manager, and a charging project developer.
It’s a tough market to walk into. VinFast, the local all-electric automaker, has sold roughly 36% of every new car in Vietnam this year, more than its next five competitors combined.
From a shell company to job postings
Tesla quietly registered Tesla Motors Vietnam LLC in Ho Chi Minh City on September 11, with about 77.7 billion dong (roughly $3 million) in charter capital and a business scope covering car imports, wholesale, and retail. Tesla never commented on it.
Now we have the first confirmation from someone inside the company. Ricky Ip, who recruits for Tesla, posted on X this morning:
