Tesla is officially coming to Vietnam – and we're hiring. Our mission is to build a world of amazing abundance and we are looking for passionate people to join us in Vietnam and help make that vision a reality. Current Job Openings: Sales Manager – https://t.co/AvW3higssS … pic.twitter.com/YDZvLNmz8P — Ricky Ip (@ipwaikrazy) October 28, 2026
The five openings are Sales Manager, Service Manager, HR Business Partner, Purchasing Manager, and Project Developer, Charging. That last one is the tell. You don’t hire someone to develop charging projects unless you plan to build Superchargers in the country.
Tesla has followed this playbook before in Southeast Asia. It went on a hiring spree in Thailand in September 2022 and opened orders there three months later. It started hiring in the Philippines in September 2024 and launched in early 2025. So a Vietnam launch in the next few months wouldn’t be a surprise.
There’s no word yet on pricing, models, or store locations. Oddly, the recruiting graphic features the next-generation Roadster, with fine print saying the vehicle is “for illustration purposes only.” Fair enough.
VinFast owns Vietnam
Tesla isn’t walking into an empty market. It’s walking into VinFast’s backyard.
VinFast delivered 177,697 cars in Vietnam through the first nine months of 2026, out of a national total of about 495,000. That’s about 36% of the entire car market, gas cars included. In September alone, it had 37.7% of the market.
Here’s how the year-to-date numbers stack up against the next brands:
VinFast: 177,697
Toyota: 53,978
Hyundai: 35,412
Mitsubishi: 31,932
Ford: 30,353
Kia: 23,461
Add up Toyota, Hyundai, Mitsubishi, Ford, and Kia and you get 175,136. VinFast alone beat all five of them.
And it’s already passed its full-year 2025 volume with a quarter left to go. VinFast says September was its 25th straight month as Vietnam’s best-selling car brand.
The model mix tells you a lot about the market. The VinFast VF 3, a tiny two-door electric crossover that launched at under $13,000 , is Vietnam’s best-selling vehicle so far this year. VinFast models held the top five spots in September.
The home-field advantages
VinFast builds its cars in Haiphong. Tesla would have to import everything, most likely from Giga Shanghai, and Vietnam kept passenger cars on its high-tariff list under the ASEAN-China free trade agreement.
Charging is another gap. VinFast’s sister company V-Green runs the country’s dominant charging network and announced plans this year to spend about $380 million on 99 ultra-fast charging stations. Third-party networks in Vietnam are still thin.
There is one thing working in Tesla’s favor. Vietnam just extended its registration fee exemption for battery-electric cars through the end of 2030, and that applies to imported EVs too.
And VinFast’s volume comes with an asterisk. A significant share of its deliveries go to GSM, the Xanh SM electric taxi and ride-hailing company founded by VinFast chairman Pham Nhat Vuong. VinFast has long relied on Vietnam for the bulk of its deliveries, which we pointed out when it delivered nearly 100,000 EVs in 2024 .

Another Big Airline Turns to Domestically-Produced Sustainable Fuel
7 photos
Photo: Singapore Airlines
Singapore Airlines (SIA) has officially agreed to purchase a considerable quantity of SAF (sustainable aviation fuel) from Aether, a startup with offices in the United States and South East Asia. The SAF will be produced in Singapore, at Aether’s brand-new Project Beacon.
SIA is now officially the first airline to purchase SAF from Project Beacon, a new commercial production facility that is still under development at a refining complex on Pulau Bukom, Singapore. Aether was incubated just a few years ago, in 2022, by Xora, a deep tech venture firm backed by Temasek.
The startup, which describes itself as a climate technology company, operates a research and development hub in Chicago, as well as an extended team in Singapore. At the beginning of last year, when Aether and SIA first signed a MoU (memorandum of understanding) regarding a regular SAF supply, Aether hadn’t even decided upon the location of its first production facility.
Now, when the final purchase agreement became official, Aether is already working on Project Beacon, the facility that will make SAF right there in Singapore. There are many types of SAF, and many ways to produce it. Aether’s proprietary Aurora technology claims to increase production efficiency while reducing capital cost.
SAF will be obtained from feedstock, but instead of the conventional HEFA (hydro-processed esters and fatty acids), it will rely on the Fischer-Tropsch process that converts gases derived from waste into liquid fuel. Aether claims that its proprietary technology results in “near-ideal” carbon conversion efficiency, while also using a more diverse range of feedstocks.
Project Beacon is only the beginning. Aether plans to being operating its first large-scale commercial facility, with a capacity ten times greater than Beacon right now, by 2031. The SAF that will be produced at Beacon is certified under the Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (CORSIA) and will be blended with conventional jet fuel according to current regulations, before being supplied to several airports served by SIA.
According to the final agreement, SIA will purchase up to 4,800 tons of SAF from Aether, over the course of three years, with first deliveries starting in 2028.
More and more major airlines and different operators are trying to secure consistent supplies of SAF, preferably from domestic sources. SAF is still considered the fastest, most reliable way of effectively reducing airplane CO2 emissions right now.
In the US, American Airlines marked one of the biggest milestones in the industry this year, with the first passenger flight powered not by SAF, but eSAF, which is the even greener version of SAF. eSAF is obtained using waste carbon and sustainable electricity.
The American Airlines eSAF flight took off from Corpus Christi International Airport (CRP) and landed at Dallas Fort Worth International Airport (DFW), powered by eSAF produced locally in Texas by Infinium.

Los Angeles police recovered approximately $1 million in stolen railroad cargo after tracing shoes advertised for sale on eBay. Investigators uncovered 35 pallets of BNSF Railroad property during an October 21 search of a local business. The merchandise included athletic footwear and backpacks from several major brands. Authorities arrested the business owner following the discovery.
The Los Angeles Police Department announced the recovery on October 26. Detectives identified DesignerDeals4Less in the 21000 block of Nordhoff Street in Chatsworth, a Los Angeles neighborhood within the San Fernando Valley. Officers discovered merchandise from Brooks, Hoka, New Balance, Adidas, ON, Salomon and JanSport. The discovery follows a separate $1 million railroad cargo recovery at a Whittier shoe retailer earlier in October.
LAPD detectives recovered 35 pallets of stolen railroad cargo valued at approximately $1 million during an October 21 search in Los Angeles. (Video: Los Angeles Police Department)
An online shoe sale leads detectives to stolen cargo
The investigation began after detectives discovered stolen Brooks/Disney collaborative shoes advertised for sale on eBay. Investigators arranged a controlled purchase, which helped establish a connection to DesignerDeals4Less. That transaction led authorities to obtain a search warrant for the Los Angeles business. In August, deputies recovered more than $123,000 in Brooks shoes following a separate BNSF boxcar burglary near Ludlow, California. Two days later, deputies recovered more than $150,000 in New Balance shoes following another BNSF boxcar burglary near Daggett, California. Authorities have not established a connection between those recoveries and the Los Angeles investigation.
Under eBay’s stolen property policy , sellers cannot list merchandise obtained through theft. The company maintains a process for law enforcement to request records during criminal investigations. The federal INFORM Consumers Act also requires marketplaces to verify identifying information from qualifying high-volume sellers. LAPD has not disclosed whether eBay provided records or whether those federal requirements helped identify the business. FreightWaves contacted eBay to determine whether the company assisted investigators or took action against the seller’s account. The company had not responded before publication.
Detectives contacted the business owner while executing the warrant on October 21. According to LAPD, the individual acknowledged purchasing stolen railroad merchandise through unauthorized distribution sources. Police identified him as Heros Tasci, 51, of Simi Valley, California. Officers arrested Tasci and transported him to Van Nuys Jail. Tasci is presumed innocent unless proven guilty in court.
Authorities booked Tasci under California Penal Code Section 496(a), which addresses receiving stolen property. The department has not announced additional arrests connected to this investigation. Police have not publicly identified the distributors who supplied the merchandise.
Multiple agencies participate in cargo theft investigation
The LAPD Commercial Crimes Division’s Cargo Theft Task Force coordinated the operation alongside several law enforcement partners. BNSF Police, Union Pacific Railroad Police and Alameda Belt Line Police participated in the investigation. Los Angeles Port Police and Los Angeles World Airport Police also assisted. Homeland Security Investigations joined the Los Angeles District Attorney’s Office Bureau of Investigation in supporting the operation. The recovery follows a separate BNSF train burglary in Colton, California , where police recovered approximately $54,000 in stolen Hot Wheels merchandise.
BNSF Railway declined to comment on the specific investigation when contacted by FreightWaves. “These criminal acts disrupt the movement of goods, increase costs for consumers and businesses,” BNSF stated. The company also emphasized its ongoing collaboration with law enforcement to combat cargo theft.
LAPD has not disclosed when or where the merchandise was originally stolen from BNSF trains. Authorities have not publicly identified those responsible for the thefts. Investigators also have not confirmed how many shipments contributed to the recovered inventory. The department has not explained how the products reached DesignerDeals4Less. FreightWaves contacted LAPD for additional details but had not received a response before publication.
The investigation remains ongoing, with detectives seeking additional information about the stolen merchandise. Anyone with relevant details can contact LAPD’s Commercial Crimes Division at 213-486-8766. Investigators accept calls during regular business hours, from 6 a.m. until 4 p.m. Anonymous tipsters can also contact Crime Stoppers at 800-222-8477.
Why it matters
Stolen freight can reenter commercial distribution channels through businesses purchasing merchandise from unauthorized sources. This recovery highlights how investigators can trace stolen products through online marketplaces and identify additional cargo.

A Ford team member inspects a Fathom unicasting (Image: Ford)
Ford has now produced more than 5,000 large aluminum “unicastings” for the Fathom, its upcoming $28,350 midsize electric pickup, as it fine-tunes the process ahead of a 2027 launch.
Each truck gets two of them, front and rear, replacing 146 individual parts. It’s the clearest sign yet that Ford is all-in on the manufacturing approach Tesla popularized with its Giga Press six years ago.
Inside Ford’s unicasting process
The update comes from Vladimir Bogachuk, Ford’s chief engineer of advanced vehicle structure architecture, in a post on Ford’s From the Road blog . The castings are made at Ford’s Shelbyville Technical Center and shipped to Louisville Assembly Plant for process testing and prototype builds. Louisville is the Kentucky factory Ford is retooling for the Fathom and other vehicles on its Universal EV Platform .
A Fathom unicasting at Ford’s Shelbyville Technical Center (Image: Ford)
Ford melts aluminum ingots at about 1,300°F (700°C) and injects the metal into either a front or rear structure mold. Once a robot pulls the part out, it goes into a quench tank, gets trimmed and machined, and then runs a gauntlet of checks: industrial X-ray scans for pores and voids, dimensional measurements in a climate-controlled room, optical surface scans, and lab tensile and chemistry tests on samples.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Machining a Fathom unicasting after it comes out of the casting machine (Image: Ford)
Nothing ships to Louisville until a batch clears every inspection. Ford says it’s also working on cutting cycle time and on designing the castings for “modular repairability.”
Every batch is held until it clears inspections, including industrial X-ray scans (Image: Ford)
That last part has been the main reason why automakers have been reticent about larger cast parts. Repair cost is the biggest knock on giant castings, since a damaged one-piece structure can turn a moderate crash into a write-off. Lucid executive Cory Steuben has said insurance concerns drove the company’s decision to skip gigacasting altogether.
Tesla started it with 70 parts
Tesla kicked this off in 2020 with the first IDRA Giga Press at Fremont, a machine with roughly 6,000 tons of clamping force. It cast the Model Y’s rear underbody in a single piece , replacing 70 parts, and Elon Musk said the change removed the need for about 300 robots.
Tesla wanted to go much further. It added a front casting, tied the two together with a structural battery pack, and moved to even bigger presses for the Cybertruck. But in 2024, Reuters reported that Tesla had backed away from its plan to cast nearly the entire underbody in one piece, and the automaker has reportedly since dropped the front casting on some Model Y production.
So Ford’s 146-to-2 figure looks great on paper. But it’s a front-and-rear layout, basically the same architecture Tesla launched with on the Model Y. Ford isn’t leapfrogging Tesla here. It’s catching up, just with a vehicle that will cost less than any Tesla on sale.
Ford has now produced more than 5,000 Fathom unicastings (Image: Ford)
The industry went bigger, but not everyone
Since that first Giga Press, a growing list of automakers have bought huge presses or committed to them:
Volvo started EX60 production at Torslanda this year with a single rear megacasting, and it ordered two 9,000-ton-class IDRA presses for its new plant in Slovakia.
Xiaomi runs 9,100-ton presses, combining 72 components into one underbody casting.
Xpeng casts the G6’s front and rear underbody, merging more than 300 parts across the two.
Honda is installing six 6,100-ton presses at its Anna Engine Plant in Ohio for EV components.
Toyota has shown its own gigacasting process, and group supplier Aisin plans to spend $3.4 billion over three years.

Others aren’t buying it. Stellantis has said it won’t invest in gigacasting, while BMW and Mercedes-Benz have stuck with smaller presses for body parts. Hyundai pushed its “Hypercasting” plan back two years.
Electrek’s Take
We’ve been tracking this casting race since Tesla’s first Giga Press showed up in Fremont, and the lesson so far is simple. Fewer parts is great, but the press alone doesn’t make a car cheap. The whole factory does.
That’s why Ford’s approach is worth watching. The unicastings are one piece of a bigger overhaul at Louisville, where Ford is splitting the line into three branches (front, rear, and the battery pack with the interior floor) that meet at the end. Ford says that can be up to 40% faster than its current assembly, or about 15% net once it reinvests some of the savings into automation and insourcing. It’s very close to the logic behind Tesla’s “unboxed” process, and they are betting it’s what actually gets you to a $28,350 truck.

Growth portfolio products like Leqembi and Spinraza helped drive Biogen to $2.8 billion in revenue for the third quarter.
The bridge to growth that Biogen CEO Chris Viehbacher has been promising has officially reached the other side. The neuroscience specialist notched a third straight quarter of revenue growth, with $2.8 billion collected for the most recent period.
Biogen in its third quarter earnings release pointed to the growth portfolio—which includes the Alzheimer’s disease therapy Leqembi and spinal muscular atrophy antisense oligonucleotide Spinraza—which jumped 49% year-over-year for $1.26 billion. Also contributing were new products from Apellis, which Biogen acquired in March for $5.6 billion. The third quarter marked the first full period of earnings from that acquisition.
“Our third quarter results demonstrate that Biogen has returned to growth,” Viehbacher said in a prepared statement.
Analysts had been expecting a slight beat of $2.6 billion on revenue and $2.14 earnings per share, which landed at $2.62, although recent acquired in-process research and development charges brought that down to a 14-cent loss when adjusted.
“Overall, a solid quarter that reinforces confidence in execution and early Apellis integration,” Truist Securities wrote Wednesday morning. “That said, with earnings increasingly taking a back seat to the pipeline, we expect clinical catalysts to dominate BIIB shares over the next ~12-14 months.”
Spinraza took in $461 million for the quarter, which Biogen attributed to accelerated conversions to a high-dose regimen that exceeded company expectations in all markets. Leqembi also continued its slow climb, adding $202 million, representing 67% growth year-over-year. Sales within the U.S. for the Alzheimer’s med were $107 million.
Apellis’ eye injection Syfovre and complement inhibitor Empaveli combined for $243 million as compared to consensus of $216.8 million.
Biogen slightly raised the lower end of its guidance to $12.20-$13, compared to $12-13 previously. Full year revenue is expected to land between $10.19-10.58 billion, Jefferies noted on Wednesday.
The big biotech will host a conference call at 8:30 am ET.
